outcome: No result found since 26 January 2024 that classifies quadratic forms over algebraic number fields, or settles a case of that classification; the general problem remains open (with Hasse's local-global classification for the equivalence question over specific completions/fields still the classical partial resolution predating the window). Ongoing research in this window (universality criteria, representation of integers, Pythagoras numbers) addresses related but distinct questions, not the classification itself.
summary: Hilbert's eleventh problem, as stated by Kaplansky and echoed in the Wikipedia bullet, asks to classify quadratic forms over algebraic number fields. Hasse's local-global (Hasse-Minkowski) solution to the equivalence/classification question for forms over number fields, via completions, dates to the 1920s and is long predates the 26 January 2024 frozen revision — it is background, not a result in the window. I searched broadly for any 2024-2026 work that advances the classification question itself (arXiv listings, general web search, the Wikipedia article's current text, and a June 2026 Simons Foundation retrospective on the status of all 23 Hilbert problems). The Simons Foundation piece (published 2026-06-18) explicitly revisits Problem 11 and states only that 'Helmut Hasse solved the problem in one context, but work has continued in others,' with no claim of any new resolution or case settled since 2024 — it corroborates the classical status quo rather than reporting a new event. The live Wikipedia article likewise shows no post-2024 update to its history/status section (last substantive edit predates the window) beyond noting older work by Cogdell, Piatetski-Shapiro and Sarnak on representation questions. Papers found in the 2024-2025 window (e.g. arXiv:2410.22507 on 'universality criterion sets for quadratic forms over number fields,' arXiv:2403.07171 on representing integers by generalized quadratic forms over quadratic fields, and work on Pythagoras numbers for infinite algebraic fields) study representation and universality properties of specific quadratic forms — these are related problems in the same subfield, not restrictions/cases of the classification question itself, so per the scope rule (§3.1) they do not count as movement on this bullet. No AI involvement was found in any of this work; none of the papers surveyed mention any AI system's role in producing results, and no AI-related claim about this problem appears anywhere in my searches. I therefore agree with the triage verdict of 'none' and did not find anything the triage missed.
competing_reading: One could argue the classical Hasse-Minkowski local-global principle, since it is the mechanism by which 'equivalence' of quadratic forms over number fields is actually decided, effectively resolves the core classification question and the bullet should be `open_stale` rather than `open`. I did not adopt this reading because (a) Hasse's result predates the frozen revision by a century and would in any case be `open_stale`, not a change in this window, and (b) the Wikipedia bullet and the broader literature (including the 2026 Simons Foundation piece) still describe the problem as only 'resolved for some cases' rather than fully classified — full classification (e.g., over general number fields with all invariants, not just via local behavior) is treated as incomplete by working number theorists, so `open` (with nothing new in the window) is the more accurate status regardless.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or announcement, dated after 26 January 2024, that gives a complete classification of quadratic forms over a general algebraic number field (or resolves a previously-unclassified case, such as extending classification results to a broader class of fields or forms) — as opposed to work on universality, representation, or Pythagoras numbers, which are adjacent questions.
